articles.author: Matthew Trueblood
articles.title: Matt Shaw to the Yankees? How Cubs Could Pursue a Controllable Starter in a Surprise Trade
articles.take: Argues Bohm's move to Kansas City leaves the Yankees desperate at third, and that Shaw or Ramírez plus a fringe prospect, with the Cubs eating McMahon's $16M, could land Will Warren. The logic is tight: Shaw is blocked, Warren is controllable and proven over 156 innings. It's a proposal, not a report, but it's the best trade idea anyone has floated for this club.

articles.author: Jordan Campbell
articles.title: 3 new targets Cubs should pursue, 2 they should avoid after $240 million spending spree
articles.take: Pushes Itoh, Griffin and Gary Sánchez, and says skip Kelly and Zac Gallen. Two of the three targets signed elsewhere by dinner, which says more about the market's speed than the list. The Kelly call is the weak spot: 'a year early' ignores that there's no other catcher left.

articles.author: Matthew Trueblood
articles.take: Real reporting, not a wish list: the Cubs are in on Itoh, Nick Martinez and Foster Griffin, one more arm comes before the lockout and a one-year add after it, and they won't give a catcher three years. The reporting holds up. The plan it describes is the problem: refusing three years on Kelly in a market with no other starting catcher is a principle that costs wins.
articles.title: Cubs Working to Add One More Starter, Address Catching Corps Before Lockout Hits

articles.author: Michael Baumann
articles.take: Baumann's argument: Rogers is fine at the price, but he's not an ace and maybe not a No. 2. His fastball edge over the average lefty fell from 1.8 mph in 2021 to 0.3 mph in 2026, and the 2025 ERA bakes upside into the price that may not be there. The title is the point, and it's correct. One Rogers doesn't fix a staff that loses five of seven 70-inning pitchers.
articles.title: Cubs Sign Trevor Rogers, Still Need About Six Other Pitchers Like Him

articles.author: Jordan Bastian
articles.take: Bastian lays out the new picture: Sato in right, Shaw the front-runner in left, Ramírez to DH or utility, and a projected lineup with Sato hitting third. He says the Cubs need at least one more starter, preferably two, and names Holmes, Peterson and Boyd as reunion options. Useful and accurate. It's a map, not an argument.
articles.title: Looking at Cubs' roster needs after Sato, Rogers deals

articles.author: Eric Samulski
articles.take: The best scouting read on Sato so far. Samulski gives both sides with numbers: the 18.4% barrel rate and NPB-best hard-hit rate, against a 17.3% swinging-strike rate and a nearly 36% chase rate. His case that the Cubs' low team strikeout rate can absorb Sato's is the right one.
articles.title: Cubs agree to six-year deal with Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato: Where he fits in Chicago's 2027 lineup

column.title: The list is shrinking faster than the Cubs are
column.dek: Rogers and Sato went official Wednesday. By dinner, three of the arms the Cubs were supposed to choose from had picked other teams. Itoh is now the whole plan.

p: Wednesday started well. The Cubs made it official: Trevor Rogers on five years and $120 million, Teruaki Sato on six years and $120 million, both on the 40-man roster by the afternoon. That's the good news, and it's real. Rogers was a 101 ERA+ and 2.2 bWAR pitcher in 2026, with a 2.90 ERA over his last 20 starts. Sato is a 27-year-old Triple Crown winner. Those were the two biggest needs on the board, and both got filled by players in their primes.
Then the rest of the day happened, and it was all bad for the North Side.

body.h: Three doors closed in three hours
p: Matthew Trueblood reported Wednesday morning that the Cubs were in on three starters for the second rotation spot: Hiromi Itoh, Nick Martinez and Foster Griffin. By the evening, Griffin was back in Cleveland on three years and $48 million. Kevin Gausman, the deadline rental, took one year and $25 million from Detroit. David Peterson, the other Cubs starter Jesse Rogers said was 'in play' just a day earlier, went home to Colorado for two years and $32 million.

Take them one at a time and none of them is a disaster. Griffin at $16 million a year is full price for a lefty who tops out around 91 and had a 5.19 ERA after the trade. Gausman at $25 million for his age-36 season is a number only a team with no plan pays. Peterson at $16 million a year is more than MLBTR's projection by a third. If the Cubs looked at those prices and said no, fine.

But you can't say no to everyone. Put them together and the fallback list is now Itoh, Martinez, Clay Holmes, Tyler Mahle and Matthew Boyd. Michael King looks headed back to San Diego: Kevin Acee says the Padres are closing in on at least one of the top starters left. The market didn't wait, and it isn't going to.

Itoh had multiple three-year offers as of Tuesday night and was expected to decide as early as Wednesday. He hasn't, which means the Cubs still have a shot. They should take it. He's 29. He has a deep pitch mix and real control. Cubbies Crib's Jordan Campbell points out his NPB numbers were better than Shota Imanaga's were when Imanaga came over. The worry is the ball: a 5-foot-9 pitcher without velocity can't afford to lose movement on the MLB ball. That's a real risk. It's also priced in. Three years at mid-rotation money is not a bet that sinks a franchise.

What would sink this offseason is waking up on Dec. 2 with Rogers, a 5.96-ERA Edward Cabrera, a Justin Steele who hasn't made an MLB start since April 2025, and Javier Assad. Sahadev Sharma said they need two more 'no-doubt' arms. They're about to have zero, with one week left.

body.h: The trade nobody is talking about
p: Trueblood's other piece Wednesday is the smartest idea on the board. The Yankees lost Alec Bohm to Kansas City and still need a right-handed third baseman. The Cubs have two, Matt Shaw and Pedro Ramírez, blocked by Alex Bregman for the next four years. New York has a spare starter in Will Warren: 156 innings in 2026, controlled through 2030, still optionable.

Trueblood's version has the Cubs taking Ryan McMahon's $16 million for 2027 to make it work. Do it. McMahon is a bad contract with one year left. Warren is the young, cheap, controllable arm this front office keeps saying it wants and never gets. The Cubs have spent the winter saying every chip should buy pitching. Shaw is a chip. This is pitching.

body.h: The catcher line still looks wrong
p: Gary Sánchez went to Miami for one year and $6.5 million on Wednesday. That was the cheap bat-first option. Carson Kelly is still out there, still the best catcher left, and the Cubs still won't go three years. Campbell argues it's better to let a player go a year early than a year late. Fair in a normal market. This is not a normal market: Ryan Jeffers took the qualifying offer, Tyler Stephenson went home, and the next-best option is Amaya and Joey Bart. Kelly was 8th of 77 catchers in ABS challenge success. Pay the third year.

The Cubs did the hard part this week. They bought the top lefty and the top bat. But a contender's offseason isn't graded on two signings. It's graded on whether the rotation can get through 162 games, and right now it can't. MLB sued the union Wednesday to protect a lockout that starts Tuesday. Nothing gets easier after that. Sign Itoh, call Cashman about Warren, and pay Kelly. Do two of the three and this is a B+ winter. Do none and the $240 million just bought a nicer version of last year's problem.

items.name: Pete Crow-Armstrong
items.note: Unanimous NL MVP. 45 HR, 41 SB, NL-best .942 OPS, MLB-best 10.6 fWAR. Hank Aaron Award, All-MLB First Team, Platinum Glove.

items.name: Seiya Suzuki
items.note: 131 OPS+, career-best 5.1 bWAR, Gold Glove finalist.

items.name: Alex Bregman
items.note: 5.8 bWAR, NL Gold Glove at third, All-MLB Second Team, ninth in MVP voting. Hitless in October.

items.name: Michael Conforto
items.note: 118 OPS+ on a minor-league deal.

items.name: Carson Kelly
items.note: 97 OPS+ and 1.9 bWAR from a catcher is a win.

items.name: Michael Busch
items.note: 106 OPS+ at first base. The walks carried him.

items.name: Ian Happ
items.note: 103 OPS+, 189 strikeouts, platooned by September.

items.name: Miguel Amaya
items.note: 98 OPS+, propped up by a .315 BABIP.

items.name: Pedro Ramírez
items.note: Held short together at 22. The xwOBA says he was lucky.

items.name: Nico Hoerner
items.note: 84 OPS+. The xBA says he deserved better; the glove is elite.

items.name: Matt Shaw
items.note: 102 OPS+ with a .303 xwOBA. Still looking for a position.

items.name: Dansby Swanson
items.note: His worst year as a Cub at the plate (90 OPS+). The glove saved the grade.

items.name: Ben Brown
items.note: 228 ERA+ over 68 innings before the neck gave out. Neck surgery Nov. 9; back around midseason.

items.name: David Peterson
items.note: 114 ERA+ after the June trade. Signed with Colorado Nov. 25 (2 yr, $32M).

items.name: Shota Imanaga
items.note: 32 starts and a 112 ERA+. The 35 homers keep it from an A.

items.name: Matthew Boyd
items.note: 108 ERA+ in 22 starts, then two first-inning homers in Game 1.

items.name: Javier Assad
items.note: 3.63 ERA, 4.92 FIP. The defense did him favors.

items.name: Ryan Rolison
items.note: 135 ERA+ in middle relief from a waiver claim.

items.name: Colin Rea
items.note: 137 innings at a 97 ERA+. Exactly what he is.

items.name: Jacob Webb
items.note: Nine saves, eight blown.

items.name: Kevin Gausman
items.note: 4.83 ERA and 0.1 bWAR after the deadline deal. Signed with Detroit Nov. 25 (1 yr, $25M).

items.name: Clay Holmes
items.note: 1.55 ERA over his first five starts, 8.24 over his last four.

items.name: Edward Cabrera
items.note: 71 ERA+, -1.4 bWAR, left off the Wild Card roster.

items.name: Jameson Taillon
items.note: 25 homers in 76 innings, -0.9 bWAR.

items.name: The bullpen
items.note: 28 blown saves, a third of inherited runners scored, 14 different save-getters.

items.name: Sato signing (6 yr, $120M, official Nov. 25)
items.note: The best bat on the market at 27, for $20M a year. The contact rate is the risk; the Cubs' lineup can carry it.

items.name: Rogers signing (5 yr, $120M, official Nov. 25)
items.note: Fair price for the best lefty left. It's an A only if a second starter follows by Dec. 1.

items.name: Losing Taira to Toronto (5 yr, $80M)
items.note: The priority target from day one, at a fair price with no picks attached. Toronto got him.

items.name: No three-year catcher deals (per Trueblood)
items.note: Cost them Stephenson and probably Kelly in a market with no third option. Amaya and Bart is the result.

items.name: Second starter still unsigned (Griffin, Gausman, Peterson gone)
items.note: None of the three prices was a bargain, but standing still while the list empties is how you end up with Holmes. Itoh is the last good fit.

items.name: Crow-Armstrong extension (6 yr, $115M)
items.note: The reigning unanimous MVP at about $19M a year through 2032. The best contract in baseball.

items.name: Bregman signing (5 yr, $175M)
items.note: 5.8 bWAR in year one. Years four and five are the risk.

items.name: Conforto minor-league deal
items.note: 118 OPS+ for almost nothing.

items.name: Peterson trade
items.note: 114 ERA+ in 15 starts.

items.name: Hoerner extension (6 yr, $141M)
items.note: Paying a glove-first second baseman through his age-35 season.

items.name: Gausman trade
items.note: A deadline splash worth 0.1 bWAR.

items.name: Cabrera trade (Caissie + 2)
items.note: The No. 1 prospect for 80 innings of 5.96 ERA.

items.name: Holmes trade (Rojas)
items.note: A top-two prospect for nine starts, zero postseason innings, and he opted out.

items.name: Bullpen construction
items.note: Hoyer's own words: 'I did a poor job on the bullpen this year, full stop.'

items.name: Kelly option declined ($1.5M buyout)
items.note: The right call on a mutual option. It only stays a B if they re-sign him or find a real starter.

items.name: Suzuki qualifying offer
items.note: Paid off as planned: he rejected it Tuesday, so the Cubs get a pick after the fourth round when he signs elsewhere.

items.name: No QO for Happ
items.note: He'd likely have taken $23.15M. Saying no was the disciplined call.

items.name: No QO for Boyd
items.note: A 36-year-old No. 5 isn't worth the risk of an acceptance.

items.name: Rea, Harvey, Thielbar options declined
items.note: $2.5M in buyouts to clear three arms that didn't miss bats or didn't pitch.

items.name: Assad option declined ($3.3M)
items.note: Saves about $1M through arbitration and keeps a useful swingman. Small, correct, and an honest read of a 4.92 FIP.

items.name: Webb restructure
items.note: Same $2.5M guarantee and a 2028 option. Smart, small.

items.name: Orze waiver claim
items.note: A 5.66 ERA with no options left. A free look, nothing more.

items.name: Sitting out Skubal (per Sharma)
items.note: Fine at $450M and $50M a year. Rogers a day later shows the money had a plan. One more arm by Dec. 1 and it's a B.

items.name: Internal plan for LF, RF and C (per Hawkins)
items.note: Hawkins admits the risk: unproven corners to pay for 'proven guys in other spots.' Fine as a trade-off. It stays a C- until those proven guys exist.

items.name: Kanzler replaced (Ben Martin, farm director)
items.note: Fast, internal and sensible. Adding Rylan Domingues on the pitching-analytics side is the right department.

items.name: Wiggins, McCullough added to the 40-man
items.note: Protects the Detmers trade chip and a Double-A arm with a 27.7% K rate. Correct and routine.

items.name: This offseason so far
items.note: Rogers and Sato, now official, lift it from a C. Losing Taira caps it, and three more starters off the board Wednesday drags it. Itoh by Dec. 1 plus Kelly makes it a B+. Neither and it's a C+.

items.name: Holmes reunion interest (per Hawkins)
items.note: They traded a top prospect for nine starts, he opted out, and the GM wants him back at a projected three years. Only a one-year swingman deal gets this off a D.

items.name: Justin Lawrence (likely minor-league deal)
items.note: Free Triple-A depth with a 5.34 career ERA and a walk problem. Harmless, and not the impact arm.

items.name: Missing the Mariners' starter sale
items.note: Seattle wanted a third baseman and a right-handed bat, the Cubs had both to spare, and Kansas City got Miller and Evans. Dipoto now says 'zero' more.

items.name: McDermott waiver claim
items.note: Free, uses an empty roster spot, 30.5% minor-league K rate. Also a 14.6% walk rate and no options. Depth, not help.

items.name: Bart waiver claim
items.note: An 82 OPS+ backup for about $3M is fine. As the Kelly replacement it's a D.

items.name: Roxby for cash
items.note: Optionable arm with a 94.6 mph heater for nothing. Smarter than another out-of-options claim.

items.name: Arias, Roberts non-tendered
items.note: Correct roster math. Leaves the backup infield thin.

grades.sub: Season grades for the regulars, the staff and the front office. Updated Nov. 25 (evening). On game days this becomes a post-game report card.
grades.title: 2026 final report card

regressionNotes.571948: His ERA beat his peripherals by more than a run.
regressionNotes.592332: He pitched better than the ERA, but 11 homers in 50 1/3 innings did the damage.
regressionNotes.592791: xFIP normalizes homers. Taillon's homer problem (25 in 76 IP) was real.
regressionNotes.608324: xSLG .391 vs. .464 actual. The power is the part most likely to fade.
regressionNotes.650644: 1.72 ERA vs. a 4.13 xFIP in 36 2/3 innings. A swingman, not a late-inning answer.
regressionNotes.663423: A 15.8% K rate. That ERA belonged to the defense.
regressionNotes.663538: The one regular who was unlucky. A .296 xBA says the average comes back.
regressionNotes.664023: Small gap. The .218 is mostly him.
regressionNotes.665795: xFIP says unlucky; an 8th-percentile xERA says hitters crushed him. Don't bank on a big bounce.
regressionNotes.665804: A .315 BABIP for a catcher. Expect the OBP to slip.
regressionNotes.669020: Middle-relief ERA, back-end peripherals. Fine in low leverage.
regressionNotes.673548: The expected line is still well above average. Price him on that, not the surface numbers.
regressionNotes.676962: Still very good, just not 228-ERA+ good.
regressionNotes.691718: Even after the haircut, a .372 xwOBA is elite.
regressionNotes.699393: The largest gap on the team. Don't pencil him into a corner spot off this line.
regressionNotes.807713: An xSLG of .353. The pop isn't real yet.
